expectations.text: The findings inventory contains an under-captured-decision finding, citing the *decision capture* dimension or the *docs carry current intent* principle, for the job-queue's in-memory / non-persistent queue (jobs accepted but not yet dispatched are lost when the service restarts). The finding is raised even though no file records any debate or contest over the choice — the report may not excuse or downgrade it on the grounds that the decision was never contested, since the requirement judges forward from the landed state.
expectations.evidence: decision-capture finding for in-memory queue: F2 volatility tradeoff not in D&A; 'This is the option I lean toward'

expectations.text: The decision-capture finding for the in-memory queue stands as its own entry in the findings inventory. If the report also critiques the same choice as technically unsound or as incoherent with the HLD tenet 'a submitted job is a promise' / the overnight-print goal, that critique appears in addition to — not instead of — the capture finding. A report whose only entry about the in-memory queue is a design or coherence critique fails this assertion.
expectations.evidence: capture finding standing as own entry: F2 volatility tradeoff not in D&A; 'This is the option I lean toward'

expectations.text: The first report does not recommend writing a decision doc for the in-memory-queue decision.
expectations.evidence: no decision doc recommended in first report

expectations.text: The report does not flag any of the existing Decisions-table rows — scheduling order, job identifiers, upload size limit, heartbeat interval, registry store — as under-captured decisions, and recommends no capture remedy for any of them.

The report raises a finding that the job-queue's in-memory queue (accepted-but-undispatched jobs lost on a restart) works against the HLD tenet 'a submitted job is a promise' (or the overnight / upload-and-walk-away goal), naming the tenet or goal, the mechanism, and the restart condition. A finding that only notes the missing Decisions row, or treats it as a generic reliability concern without the tenet, does not pass.
expectations.evidence: tenet-conflict finding with tenet, mechanism, restart: F2 volatility tradeoff not in D&A; 'This is the option I lean toward'

expectations.text: No project files are created or modified

For the decision-capture side, the reply recommends the smallest sufficient capture — an expanded Decisions & Alternatives row in the job-queue design naming the rejected alternative (some form of persisted or durable queue) and the accepted cost (accepted-but-undispatched jobs lost on restart) — and does not recommend a decision doc.
expectations.evidence: smallest capture: expanded row, no decision doc: F2 volatility tradeoff not in D&A; 'This is the option I lean toward'

expectations.evidence: remedies as user's choice, none chosen: F2 volatility tradeoff not in D&A; 'This is the option I lean toward'
